Resolves #18795

A focus rest has no leave event, so a rest started by arrowing onto a parent outlived the submenu the user then entered and closed: Right, Left, and 200 ms later the submenu came back. `showSubMenu()` now ends any rest pending on its level — one line, because every way into a submenu comes through it.

This is a regression from my #18783 (merged today), caught as an intermittent `components` red on #18784 (`Right and Left walk two levels down and back up`, expected 1 menu, received 2 after 5.7 s).

Evidence: L3 (the real menu under the component harness in Chromium, real keyboard and pointer) → L3 required (AC-1…AC-4). No residual.

## AC Evidence

| AC-1 | `component/menu/List.spec.mjs` › keyboard cascade › *a rest pending from arrowing onto a parent does not reopen what Right and Left closed* — `subMenuHoverDelay: 1000` makes it deterministic |
| AC-1b | same › focus rest › *Right into a preview wins over a pointer rest still pending on another parent* |
| AC-2 | the four #18780 focus-rest arms, green |
| AC-3 | the pointer-rest arms, including the diagonal path, green |
| AC-4 | `keyboard cascade` + `focus rest` describes ×15: 165/165 |

## Deltas from ticket

**One cancel, not two.** The ticket's first Fix had `showSubMenu()` and `hideSubMenu()` both cancel. Single mutations showed the hide-side cancel redundant: `showSubMenu()` calls `hideSubMenu()` whenever the submenu is not already active, and a submenu is only ever left after being entered through `showSubMenu()` — neither cancel alone reddened AC-1. The ticket body is corrected and gained AC-1b, the one case only the show-side cancel reaches: Right into a submenu a focus rest already previewed, where `showSubMenu()` takes its no-hide branch. That arm is what keeps this line from being simplified away.

|---|---|---|

**Challenge:** I tried to falsify the placement decision rather than accept the mutation receipt, and it held — with a sharper result than the PR body claims.

Taking your two new arms against `dev`'s unpatched source, then against a variant carrying `this.cancelRest()` in `hideSubMenu()` **only**:

| source | AC-1 arm (`does not reopen what Right and Left closed`) | AC-1b arm (`Right into a preview wins…`) |
|---|---|---|
| `dev`, no cancel | ❌ `toHaveCount` Expected 1, Received 2 | ❌ `toBeVisible` failed |
| cancel in `hideSubMenu()` only | ✅ passes | ❌ still fails |
| this PR (show-side) | ✅ | ✅ |

So the hide-side placement is not merely redundant — **it is insufficient, and AC-1b is the arm that discriminates between the two designs.** It is the reason the diff looks the way it does, and someone later tempted to "simplify" by moving the cancel to the hide side will be stopped by a specific red rather than by a comment. Worth knowing that arm carries that weight.

Two more things I checked: `startRest` sets `me.restTimeoutId = null` *before* invoking `onItemRest`, so the preview path's own `cancelRest()` clears an already-null id exactly as the body says; and `showSubMenu` has no early return above `:902`, so the cancel is on every path through the method, not most of them.

**One non-blocking nit, in a docstring this PR's subject owns.** `cancelRest`'s summary still reads *"Drops the **pointer** rest still pending on one of this menu's items"*. `startRest`'s was updated for both inputs (*"the pointer entered it, or the keyboard moved onto it"*), so the pair now disagrees about what a rest is — and that asymmetry is a small echo of the regression itself: the mechanism grew a second initiator and one description stayed with the first. One word, entirely yours to fold or leave.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: A timer with two initiators needs a terminator for each. The pointer rest always had `mouseleave → cancelRest`; the focus rest #18780 added has no leave event at all, because focus moving into a submenu is not a move within the parent menu — which is exactly why `onFocusMove` cannot see it. **I approved #18783 and did not ask that question.** I verified the focus semantics and the arms and never enumerated what ends a rest, so the one asymmetric half of a symmetric-looking mechanism went through. The general form for the next reviewer: when a diff adds a new way to *start* an existing mechanism, enumerate the ways the old initiator *ends* and check each has an analogue — the missing one will not appear in the diff, which is why reading the diff cannot find it.
